\section{Uncomputability --- Halting}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.Uncomputability.Halting
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\subsection*{Uncomputability --- Halting: Introduction}

This module establishes the uncomputability of the halting problem
[AB09, \S 1.5.1, Theorem 1.11]. It defines the halting function on the universal
machine's paired input format and proves, by history's first reduction, that a
Turing machine deciding it would make the diagonal function $\mathrm{UC}$
computable, contradicting the diagonalization theorem [AB09, Theorem 1.10].

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\subsection*{Uncomputability --- Halting: Results}

\begin{definition}[The halting function]
\lean{Complexity.HALT}
\label{Complexity.HALT}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MachineCode, Turing.pairEncode}
Fix a coding scheme $c$ that assigns to every bit string $\alpha$ a Turing machine
(the machine that $\alpha$ denotes under $c$). The halting function
$\mathrm{HALT}_c$ maps a bit string $s$ to a Boolean: $\mathrm{HALT}_c(s)$ is true
precisely when $s$ is the pairing encoding $\langle \alpha, x \rangle$ of two bit
strings --- the universal machine's input format, code first --- and the machine
denoted by $\alpha$ halts on input $x$, i.e.\ completes some output within some
finite number of steps. Strings not of this form (the pairing encoding is not
surjective) are mapped to false.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of the halting function]
\lean{Complexity.HALT_eq_true_iff}
\label{Complexity.HALT_eq_true_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.HALT, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MachineCode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c$ be a machine representation scheme and let $s$ be a bit string. The halting
function of $c$ returns true on $s$ if and only if there are bit strings $\alpha$ and
$x$ such that $s$ is their pairing encoding, and the machine decoded from $\alpha$
produces some output on input $x$ within some finite number of steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting on an encoded pair]
\lean{Complexity.HALT_pairEncode_eq_true_iff}
\label{Complexity.HALT_pairEncode_eq_true_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.HALT, Complexity.HALT_eq_true_iff, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MachineCode, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode_injective}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c$ be a machine representation scheme and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be bit strings. The
halting function of $c$ returns true on the pairing encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$ if and
only if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ produces some output on input $x$ within some
finite number of steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Computability reduction from halting to the diagonal function]
\lean{Complexity.UC_computable_of_HALT_computable}
\label{Complexity.UC_computable_of_HALT_computable}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Computable, Complexity.HALT, Complexity.HALT_pairEncode_eq_true_iff, Complexity.UC, Complexity.UC_eq_false_iff, Complexity.UC_eq_true_iff, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM.Computes, Turing.FinTM.Computes.exists_computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime.computes, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_ifEq, Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_partial, Turing.FinTM.exists_cond, Turing.computesFunInTime_pairEncode_diag, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universal}
\difficulty{5}
Let $c$ be an effective machine representation scheme, and suppose the function that
maps each bit string $s$ to the one-bit string whose bit is the halting value of $c$ on
$s$ is computable. Then the function mapping each bit string $\alpha$ to the one-bit
string whose bit is the diagonal value of $c$ at $\alpha$ is computable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uncomputability of the halting function]
\lean{Complexity.HALT_not_computable}
\label{Complexity.HALT_not_computable}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Computable, Complexity.HALT, Complexity.UC_computable_of_HALT_computable, Complexity.UC_not_computable, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode}
\difficulty{1}
For every effective machine representation scheme $c$, no finite-state Boolean Turing
machine computes the function sending each bit string $s$ to the one-bit string whose
bit is the value of the halting function of $c$ at $s$.
\end{theorem}
